passage:
A store received many returned clothes from online shoppers. Some people ordered several sizes, kept one, and returned the rest.
The shop manager explained that returns are not as simple as customers think. Returned items must be checked, repacked, cleaned, or sometimes thrown away.
In business class, students discussed convenience and hidden costs.
One student said online shopping made mistakes easier. Another said clear size charts and customer reviews could reduce returns.
The lesson was not that online shopping is bad. It was that every convenience has a path behind it.
A returned shirt does not disappear. It travels again, using time, labor, and energy.
